title: Find Products in a Price Range
real_world_story: A customer wants to see all products priced between a minimum and maximum budget. The e-commerce platform maintains product prices in sorted order so that price-based searches can be performed efficiently.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Efficiently locating the boundaries of the requested price range

problem_statement: Given a sorted array of product prices and two values L and R, find the number of products whose prices are between L and R inclusive.
task: Determine how many products fall within the customer's requested price range.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N integers representing product prices in non-decreasing order. The third line contains two integers L and R representing the minimum and maximum allowed price.
output_format: Print the number of products whose prices satisfy L <= price <= R.

examples.explanation: The prices 450, 500, 700, 900 and 900? No duplicate exists in this dataset; therefore the qualifying prices are 450, 500, 700 and 900, giving 4.

expected_algorithm.name: Binary Search
expected_algorithm.reason: Because the prices are sorted, binary search can be used to find the first and last positions belonging to the requested range without scanning the entire array.

hint: Find the first position where the price is at least L.
Find the first position where the price is greater than R.
The difference between these positions gives the number of products in the range.
real_world_takeaway: Sorted product data allows price filters to be processed much more efficiently than repeatedly scanning the entire catalog.
